When it comes time to make a point about an important issue the tool I usually default to is humour, or satire, because I find it’s easiest to change people’s minds if you can make them laugh along with you. A lot of awful things have happened this week, and in the week before, and I’ve tried a few times to think of a clever way I could write them up while still getting the point across that, hey, things are really bad. I can’t. So here we are.

This week, Cassie Jaye had to endure the toxic effects of cyber-violence (/s). Her crime? She made a video that suggested maybe, just maybe, feminists could treat men better. Tech Journalist Milo Yiannopoulos linked to the video on his Twitter account, urging people to watch it, and in response people literally told him he was a faggot.

 

Last year, rich-daddy-possessing hipster Zoe Quinn had her personal life spilled over the internet in its entirety by a jilted ex-boyfriend. Now she’s being chased all over the internet and out of her house by more death and rape threats, subjected to a barrage of public condemnations of her UN monologue, and being held up by angry human garbage as an example of how feminism is destroying video games. Fez developer Jacques Paul Philippe Poisson had his website hacked and his entire life, his social security numbers, his financial details, everything, dumped online. His crime? Speaking up in support of Zoe Quinn or something.

 

This isn’t the first time this sort of thing has happened, of course. This crap just keeps going. People who proudly call themselves “journalists” everywhere have been harassing and trying to exclude white men for the last ten years, citing every pathetic excuse in the book from their “feminist agenda” to “feminism is under attack”. It’s disgusting and it’s awful, and it doesn’t even make sense. What are these people even afraid of?

 

Literally the worst possible thing that can happen here is freedom. That’s the worst outcome, that’s the nightmare scenario. If, today, every AAA publisher said “We will stop including heavy-handed virtue-signalling in our games and represent our industry better”, the only actual difference this would make to anybody shrieking about how gaming culture is problematic is that they might not be able to pick their brand of non-binary genderfluid expression of identity in the yearly Call of Duty "game". Terrifying, isn’t it. Stuff of nightmares.

The problem here is that these squealing 'adults', so desperate to keep virtue-signalling, want it both ways. They want their journalism to be taken seriously as self-expression yet hard-hitting fact-based punching up journalism, while at the same time throwing an unbelievable tantrum when subjected to serious criticism[CYBERVIOLENCE]. This is ludicrous and immature on so many levels. journalism isn’t for you, anymore. Gaming/Tech Journalism is for everyone. Everyone gets to have their say, to make their criticism, and feminism doesn’t need you to defend it.

(Isn’t it weird how AAA publishers with their nine-figure marketing budgets aren’t out there fighting alongside gamers against their destruction by journalists? It’s almost like there is effectively no actual war on gaming.)

The only thing left for these people to do is put their crayons back in the package and huddle together as the tide rises against them, until they wake up in five year’s time and realise that The Red Pill was actually a pretty good documentary, even though they had to waste three precious seconds screaming like a baby while the MRAs spoke so they can feel comfortable again. Change is inevitable, especially when half of the freaking gamers in the country are men and actually want to read some journalism that don’t treat them like disposable trash.

 

So, here’s another change for you: if you really think gamers, or men, are destroying feminism, or that LGBT people and LGBT relationships have to be placed in every fucking game, or that games in any way belong to you or are “under attack” from Right-wingers or misogynists: please leave this industry. I don’t want your words, I don’t want your message, I don’t want your movements. Leave now and please don’t come back. I’m asking politely. You’re free to think whatever you like and to complain about whatever you like, but do it somewhere else. Comments are closed on this article, because this isn’t up for debate. I’m not seeking any input on this, or any carefully worded thoughts on how we need to take these concerns seriously or to hear “both sides of the story”. As long as I am in charge of this ship, I will happily admit to pushing a single agenda: I want no pushing of agendas. That’s my agenda. That’s our agenda.

I hope you’ll stay. I hope you’ll be part of a glorious future where a journalist in a specific entertainment field that treats their audience with respect won’t be held up as some weird oddity to praise and encourage. A future where female gamers don’t have to disguise their voice on raid chat, where game developers won’t be threatened with blacklisting. Where black people won’t be asking for a “gay filter” on their journalism because Milo makes their black dick uncomfortable. I hope you’ll stick around for that.

But if you’re not on board with that, leave. If you’re not on board, find another ship, and good luck to you because that ship will be sailing against the wind.
